summary: @servicetitan/assist-ui preinstall drops Bun runtime to execute an obfuscated bundled payload
details: The package advertises itself as a React UI-components library but ships a `preinstall` lifecycle script (`setup.mjs`) that is itself obfuscated (obfuscator.io-style identifier renaming and per-function string-lookup dictionaries hiding constants such as `ldd`, `/etc/os-release`, `Alpine`, `bun`, and the download URL). At install time the script downloads the Bun JavaScript runtime from GitHub releases (oven-sh/bun v1.3.13) into a temp directory, unzips it, chmods it executable, and invokes it via `execFileSync` against a sibling file `math_init.js` shipped in the tarball. `math_init.js` is a 727,680-byte heavily obfuscated blob (Bun-CJS header, shuffled string array with a rotator, `_0xNNNN`-style identifiers) whose filename does not reflect its content. A UI-component library has no legitimate need for an alternate JavaScript runtime or for executing an opaque bundled script at install time, and running the payload under Bun evades Node-based scanning. The combined pattern — obfuscated lifecycle script, alternate-runtime fetch, and execution of an obfuscated bundled payload on `npm install` — constitutes arbitrary code execution on the installer's machine at install time under author control.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
